answer: lotus admits a zephyr only behind a host root bound to one physical serial, and that root can anchor one zephyr ever; admission also burns vertex equal to the live zephyr count in lotus, read fresh at commit. A clone farm cannot share one machine or batch the burn, and each admission raises the next price. A thousand fakes need a thousand distinct hosts and 499,500 vertex. The bill is one host root plus vertex per zephyr, attached to each lotus admission; it fails if host roots are virtualized or resold.
